launches.body:
**TL;DR: Nine Fives makes test equipment for manufacturers of radio devices in cellphones, drones, or satellites.**

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7vtMt6-0SvY](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7vtMt6-0SvY%3C/video%3E)

**Problem:** You are a hardware engineer holding up a billion dollar satellite constellation or slipping a cellphone release date because the legacy test equipment in your production line was designed around the January 1997 revision of the USB Human Interface Device specification and the firmware hasn’t been updated since then.

Your AI agent is blissfully unaware of how this thing works because the “documentation” is hidden in a PDF on a password protected FTP server. After the legacy vendor left your email on read for a week they gave you access and sent you a [VB.NET](http://VB.NET) script that they think should work. You ran it and now all 8 of that vendor’s devices in your rack have tried to enumerate as “COM11” in device manager. Now you have 8 broken pieces of equipment instead of just 1!

**Solution:** We’re Noah Levy and Andrew Kurtz and we are building Nine Fives. Together we have spent a decade at SpaceX designing radio frequency hardware and test systems for multi-million dollar products. Our equipment is driverless, touchscreen enabled, and uses a single, machine-readable, API with both REST and SCPI endpoints.

Every module we build works as a standalone product, but if you use our rack-mountable data and power backplane then you can take advantage of our NineVue web-app for generating easy-to-maintain, machine-readable rack configuration and our [skill.md](http://skill.md) so that your AI agent can finally understand your test system and write your test software. 

**Get off the critical path and reduce your production readiness timeline from months to minutes.**

name: Arlo Industries
long_description:
Arlo Industries is building a network of sensors that precisely tracks stealthy drones and aerial threats better than radars.

This capability does not exist yet because traditional radars are built on past war doctrines designed to protect single, centralised assets. Modern warfare, however, demands wide-area, persistent coverage that is both passive and economically scalable. By utilising a mesh architecture, Arlo Industries unlocks unprecedented asymmetric economics. The network is fundamentally built to scale: the cost of adding sensors grows linearly, but the tracking accuracy increases exponentially, delivering highly resilient, persistent coverage for a fraction of the cost of legacy systems.

Deo founded Arlo Industries after spending over 6 years in the Israeli defence ecosystem, where he lived through multiple conflicts and experienced the Iron Dome and other systems in action against ICBMs and the infamous Shahed drones. Learning exactly how these defence systems could be improved after a Shahed exploded close to his apartment, he built Arlo Industries around the core philosophy that conflict should be concise & precise.

The people behind Arlo1 includes a PhD in drones and autonomy and military experts.

Arlo Industries has actively showcased this technology directly to Ukrainian militaries on the frontlines, as well as to operators across Europe and the USA.

launches.tagline: We build sensors that track drones & missiles better than radars
launches.body:
---

**Hi, I'm Deo, founder of [Arlo Industries](https://arlo1.com/).**

<https://youtu.be/2F0cugbrq3A>

**The problem**

Modern air defence depends on active radars: expensive, emitting, and targetable. A single ground-based radar unit can cost tens of millions, broadcasts its location to anything listening, and leaves massive coverage gaps against low-altitude threats like drones.

This architecture was built for a different era. Today's threat, swarms of cheap drones and cruise missiles flying below radar coverage, exploits every weakness of centralised, active sensing.

**What we're building**

Mentat is a passive, distributed sensing network.

* **Tracks aerial objects in 3D without emitting**: invisible to the threats it detects
* **Accurately track smaller threats**: our mesh works together to better pinpoint small targets
* **Scales via many low-cost nodes**: instead of a few high-value targets, we employ asymmetric economics where adding nodes grows linearly in cost but tracking accuracy increases exponentially

We're the sensing layer, the force multiplier for every interceptor and C-UAS system in the market.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101954&key=user_uploads/836806/ddbe92c9-897d-4e52-90ab-c8574ed7335c)

**What we're really building**

Drone detection is our wedge, not our ceiling. The real innovation isn't in any single sensor, it's in the network that ties it all together. We're building the foundational sensing and communications infrastructure layer for frontline defence. A distributed, resilient network that future defence technologies will plug into. Like the **Starlink before the Starship.**

**Why now**

Low-altitude airspace is increasingly contested. Ukraine, Nordics, Eastern Europe, & Middle East, operators everywhere are discovering that the cost curve of traditional radar doesn't scale against distributed drone threats. At the same time, edge compute, distributed systems, and passive optical sensing have reached the point where a fundamentally different architecture is viable.

**Backstory**

I spent 6+ years in Israel, living through multiple conflicts and seeing systems like Iron Dome operate against ballistic missiles and drones firsthand. When a Shahed drone exploded near my apartment, the gap between what exists and what's needed became personal. Since then, I've been in Ukraine and across Eastern Europe, working directly with military operators and validating in real conflict environments.

📍Field Test - Ukraine

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101954&key=user_uploads/836806/b380d961-dde4-4e50-b6eb-1cbf708e6d3c)

**Traction**

* Active technology demonstrations with Ukrainian military on the frontlines
* Partnerships and military relationships across USA, Ukraine, Finland, and Estonia.
* Team includes a PhD in drones/autonomy and military domain experts

**Our asks**

🔧 **Hiring:** We're looking for engineers in optics, signal processing, long-range comms, mesh networks, and off-grid embedded systems → [Jobs page](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/arlo-industries/jobs)

🤝 **Intros:** Defense operators, C-UAS companies, or critical infrastructure partners (airports, energy, borders) dealing with aerial awareness gaps → please reach out on [Linkedin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/deoarlo/)

launches.title: Edgerun: The 10 lb Military Exoskeleton
launches.tagline: Powered exoskeleton that assists every step a soldier takes under combat load
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Edgerun builds powered legs for soldiers. A 10 lb exoskeleton worn at the waist that adds assistance to every step and cuts the effort of moving under a combat load by 30-45%. Since May, we've run 100+ field tests with Ukrainian operators out of our Kyiv field office.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nFLeQV2DWMc>

**▍The problem**

Every system on the modern battlefield has been upgraded. The human carrying it has not.

* For 2,500 years the soldier's load sat around 40 lbs. In the last 40 years it **doubled, then doubled again**.
* A US infantryman now carries **90-140 lbs** into a fight. The Army's own field manual sets the limit at 48 lbs.
* On deployment, load carriage causes **twice as many** evacuations as enemy contact.
* The Pentagon and VA spend **$9.3B a year** on the injuries it leaves behind.

Battles are won through speed and surprise. Load kills both.

**▍Why now**

Sixty years of military exoskeletons died the same death. The device cost more to carry than it gave back. SOCOM's TALOS burned $400M before it was cancelled in 2019.

That all changed in the last 18 months. The humanoid robotics boom produced one-pound actuators that put out 30+ Nm of torque, and 21700 cells crossed 450 Wh/kg. The components finally exist. They’re getting better every quarter.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/cd255b24-3429-4270-9670-e28fc8df360b)

**▍What we built**

Our first exoskeleton is a bilateral hip system worn at the waist. It reads your gait in real time and adds torque at the moment your hip drives forward. The hip produces about 60% of the force in loaded walking, so assisting it gives the most help-per-pound of anything you could strap to the body.

* Under 10 lbs with batteries
* 30-45% less metabolic cost under a combat load
* On in 5 seconds, off in one
* 12+ hours on hot-swappable drone-class batteries
* Quasi-direct-drive actuators, composite structures, CAN bus. Nothing exotic by design.

The soldier arrives at the objective still able to fight, patrols 10 km farther, and keeps a body that lasts past one tour.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/94bf48a9-0ba6-4ce7-94a2-f467cae9657c)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/883d1e98-900a-420a-b7ff-e56cc8911c0c)

**▍Ukraine**

Our field engineers work out of a Kyiv office, alongside operators from infantry, special operations, and National Guard units who provide structured feedback every day. [Balistyka](https://balistyka.ua/), one of Ukraine's leading body armor makers, is an integration partner, helping us ensure our system fits the kit soldiers already wear.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/89a30d39-fe11-421c-abe7-32961da8d1bd)

**▍The mission**

Defense is the first customer, not the last. Read the mission at edgerun.com/mission

launches.title: Mass Magnetics: USA-made magnets

launches.body:
### **TL:DR; Mass Magnetics makes American magnets in minutes.**

🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110611&key=user_uploads/3652354/be41c9e5-378d-452f-a111-10380035f14d)

**Every electric motor runs on rare-earth magnets.** EVs, drones, robots, wind turbines, guided munitions: nearly all of them are dependent on Chinese magnets. On January 1st, 20270, [regulation changes will make it illegal to deliver anything that walks, drives, or flies to US Defense if it contains a magnet produced in covered countries like China.](https://www.massmagnetics.com/comply) The domestic supply chain meant to replace it doesn't exist yet. **Mines take a decade to permit, and the ore they pull up leaves radioactive tailings behind, making permitting magnet mining a nightmare.**

We’re[ ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/energyeric)the founders, [Eric Silver](https://x.com/metalscontent) and [Matthew Grol](https://www.linkedin.com/in/matthew-groll/)l (left and right in the pic below). We’ve known each other since grade school. Since then, Eric’s built multiple battery pilot production lines and materials science labs in the Midwest for NSF-funded companies. Matthew’s built exquisite aerospace gear including Moon-regolith melters and ultra-precise guidance systems for the world’s foremost labs at NASA, Draper, and MIT. **Together we’re making one bet: America's rare-earth problem isn't a mining problem.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110611&key=user_uploads/3652354/2046e9de-2db6-47e8-91fc-651e31e5a834)

**Mass Magnetics’ unfair advantage is sitting in end-of-life electric vehicles, hard drives, and industrial equipment.** The team uses AI models and robotics trained on real scrap to sort metallurgy by exact grade and chemistry. Then, a rapid-sintering process takes that reclaimed mass to a finished magnet in 3 minutes, where conventional approaches take over 4 hours. The result is a magnet as strong as anything imported, with no radioactive footprint or bureaucratic permitting, fully compliant for US defense.

**If you build robots, drones or motors visit our site and reach out at [outreach@massmagnetics.com](mailto:outreach@massmagnetics.com) and get your magnets.**

launches.tagline: Semiconductors to push machines where humans cant go.
launches.body:
<https://youtu.be/oHKXAeiH79Y>

**TLDR:** Synapse Semiconductor builds image sensors that process **AI on the sensor** itself. Each pixel captures light and runs neural-network computation in the same device, replacing the need for a GPU while cutting the power and latency of edge vision.\
\
\
A camera has no use by itself. Its value is only when its information gets evaluated. How can a camera that only has value when combined with a GPU support local intelligence? GPUs will get better, yet the fundamental problem is the separation of the camera and the GPU. Solving that separation will unlock bountiful innovation in machine perception. 

**RETINA: a chip designed like the human retina which runs neural network operations in the camera pixel.** 

\
We have compressed the whole edge AI vision hardware stack into **one wafer**. CNNS, VLMS, etc can run on just one chip that senses light. Our compute transistors are also the same photosensors that see light. There is no longer separation between compute (Nvidia Jetson Nano) and a camera (RealSense Depth Camera). \
\
If you are building robotic perception, drones, and vision systems for physical AI —> [book.synapsesemi.org](http://book.synapsesemi.org)

name: Rise Reforming
long_description:
Geopolitical conflicts and natural disasters frequently expose the vulnerability of the American chemical industry. The reason? Production is centralized and fossil fuel-dependent. The solution? Localized production using an undervalued resource: biogas. The US produces enough biogas to make over $20 bn/y worth of chemicals, but 60% is wasted in low-margin applications or flared altogether.

Rise Reforming is commercializing a modular process to transform this underutilized biogas on-site into cheap, supply-secure chemicals. Our beachhead market is dimethyl ether (DME), used as an aerosol propellant and a low-carbon fuel additive in propane. Our target market is methanol: an established billion $ chemical and the future of low-carbon shipping.

We're doing our pilot project at a Chicagoland wastewater plant. This will be the first wastewater biogas-to-methanol demo in the Americas.

We're hiring for a senior chemical process engineer. Apply here: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/rise-reforming/jobs/wJ9Q9nv-senior-chemical-process-engineer

name: Nori
long_description:
We manufacture Nori: A sub-$2000 bimanual mobile manipulator that can clean rooms, restock shelves, and fold clothes. Nori can handle basic tasks out of the box, and its software lets anyone teach Nori to automate work specific to their home or business. 

Nori aims to solve the robotics data bottleneck. By deploying affordable robots to customers around the world, we can gather the diverse data required to train the next generation of generalist robotic policies. Every user of Nori makes Nori smarter.

Since launching 6 weeks ago we have already deployed our first robot and have over $440k+ in sales.

We can bring general-purpose robotics to homes and businesses that could never afford it before. There are 132.7 million households and 8.4 million employer business locations in the U.S. At $1,688 per robot, selling just one Nori to 0.5% of them represents a $1.2B market opportunity in the U.S. alone.
one_liner: The most capable American-made humanoid robot for $1,688

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Robots are finally capable enough to be useful, but they're priced like cars, not appliances. A capable humanoid costs $20,000+, so general-purpose robots stay in labs and pilots instead of homes. 

It's a big problem because household labor is one of the largest unpriced markets in the world. Today's answer is a stack of single-task machines, a dishwasher, a washer, a vacuum, each $600 to $1,000 and doing exactly one thing. Whoever ships a general-purpose robot at appliance prices doesn't win a niche, they open consumer robotics the way the PC opened computing.

We're robotics researchers from Columbia (RoboPIL, CGUI). After years watching \[$100K research robots struggle with tasks cheap hardware could handle\], we realized the gap between lab robots and home robots isn't intelligence, it's cost discipline. Nobody was going to fix that from inside a lab, so we left to build it: a $1,688 robot anyone can teach.

name: Aerogen Systems
long_description:
We are building the future of chip manufacturing.

Chips are more advanced than ever, and the features inside them keep getting smaller. But the cleanroom infrastructure supporting their manufacture has not scaled at the same pace. Intel, TSMC, Samsung, and others spend billions building and operating massive cleanrooms, only to isolate their most advanced wafers from the surrounding facility as much as possible.

We think that architecture is backwards. Instead of making the entire building cleaner, why not make the machinery itself as clean as possible?

Talos is our proprietary tool-integrated purification system. It sits directly inside semiconductor equipment and continuously destroys airborne molecular contaminants before they reach the wafer. Instead of fighting contamination by constantly flooding tools with ultra-high-purity nitrogen, Talos keeps the environment inside the machine 10–100x cleaner, without the massive purge-gas bill.

Talos is powerful on its own, but it is also the foundation for a much bigger vision: the Cleanpipe.

The Aerogen Systems Cleanpipe is an ultra-clean interconnect infrastructure that protects wafers as they move from machine to machine across the fab. Rather than relying on a billion-dollar cleanroom to protect every cubic foot of factory space, Cleanpipe creates a controlled environment only where cleanliness actually matters: around the wafer.

Talos cleans the tools. Cleanpipe connects them. Eventually, we delete the cleanroom and build more advanced chips, at greater scale, with radically less infrastructure. With cleanpipes connecting tools, chip fabs can exist anywhere.
one_liner: Modernizing Chip Manufacturing Infrastructure

launches.title: Aerogen Systems: Building Chip Fabs Without Cleanrooms
launches.tagline: Redefining the architecture behind chip manufacturing
launches.body:
Hi YC!

We’re [Noah](https://www.linkedin.com/in/noahvogel/) and [Colin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/colin-lavery-67b7512a3/), the founders of [Aerogen Systems](https://www.aerogensystems.com/). We’re building the next generation of clean infrastructure for chip manufacturing.

**TL;DR:** Aerogen Systems makes semiconductor tools clean themselves. Talos, our tool-integrated purification system, continuously destroys airborne contaminants around the wafer, creating 10–100x cleaner tool environments while reducing dependence on ultra-high-purity nitrogen. Over time, Talos becomes the foundation for the Cleanpipe, an ultra-clean interconnect network that lets wafers move between tools without depending on the surrounding cleanroom.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5yBzBCzwFV8>

# **The Problem**

**Chip features keep getting smaller, but cleanrooms do not scale with them.**

Semiconductor manufacturers spend billions building enormous cleanroom facilities, then spend even more trying to isolate their most advanced wafers from the environment they just built.

As features approach the atomic scale, trace airborne contaminants that were once tolerable can create defects, reduce yield, and disrupt some of the most sensitive manufacturing processes on Earth. Yet the industry's answer has largely been more of the same: cleaner facilities, more filtration, and more ultra-high-purity nitrogen flooding sensitive equipment.

**The proof is in the yield numbers.** 2026 reporting puts Intel’s 18A program between roughly 50% and 65% yield as it pushed the node toward high-volume production. With global semiconductor sales projected to reach **$1.5 trillion** in 2026, every percentage point matters. Improvements in yield and manufacturing efficiency can represent tens of billions of dollars in value.

# **The Solution**

At Aerogen Systems, we think the industry is approaching this problem backwards.

**The whole factory does not need to be a massive cleanroom.** Only the environment immediately surrounding the wafer does.

Talos is our proprietary, tool-integrated purification system. It sits directly inside semiconductor manufacturing equipment and continuously recirculates and purifies the environment around the wafer. Instead of constantly replacing contaminated gas with more ultra-high-purity nitrogen, Talos destroys contaminants at the point of use, offering 10–100x cleaner tool environments while dramatically reducing dependence on purge gas and consumable filtration.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111026&key=user_uploads/3388722/a095a4e2-31a2-4307-b8f1-bca417cb27d7)

_1. Rendering of standalone Talos unit._

But Talos is only part of the vision.

With tool-integrated purification units as a foundation, we build **the Cleanpipe: ultra-clean interconnect infrastructure** that protects wafers as they move from machine to machine across the fab. Talos cleans the tools. The Cleanpipe connects tools to each other. Together, they delete the cleanroom and all the expenses that come with it.

# **What We’ve Built**

Talos has progressed through multiple generations of hardware development and is protected by patent-pending IP. We’ve validated the core purification architecture and are now working toward tool integrations, pilots, and commercial deployments with semiconductor manufacturers and equipment companies.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111026&key=user_uploads/3388722/a8596c2c-c29b-4271-8d92-85672dce0dc1)

_2. Test results showing Talos bringing industry-standard 6N purification levels down to 8N — a 100x improvement in cleanliness._

The next step is connecting these purified environments together through the Cleanpipe, creating an ultra-clean path around the wafer from tool to tool and ultimately removing the need to maintain the entire fab as one enormous cleanroom.

# **The Team**

Aerogen Systems started as a NASA-backed research group at the University of Michigan, where our team developed the underlying purification technology. 

We have spent the last several years designing, testing, patenting, and rebuilding this technology for extreme manufacturing environments.

* Noah, CEO, worked in manufacturing engineering at SpaceX, where he focused on production rate and yield improvement for the Starship program.


* Colin, CTO, previously built advanced particle detectors at H3D and led the team through the earliest design cycles of Talos.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111026&key=user_uploads/3388722/4db2a255-30a8-44ee-928b-b07425918094)

# **Our Ask**

We want to meet semiconductor fabs, equipment OEMs, and manufacturing teams interested in pilots, tool integrations, and commercial deployments. If this sounds like you, please reach out to [hi@aerogensystems.com](mailto:hi@aerogensystems.com)!

We are building toward a world where fabs no longer need billion-dollar cleanrooms to manufacture the world’s most advanced chips.

launches.tagline: AI-native orchestration for physical R&D testing
launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR: [Daqstra](https://www.daqstra.com/) is the AI-native test orchestration platform for physical R&D. We connect fragmented test hardware, capture every run, and give engineers an API to operate their test setup, helping aerospace, energy, and robotics teams spend less time rebuilding infrastructure.**

Hey! We’re [Anchit Kumar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/anchitk/) and [Darell Chua](https://www.linkedin.com/in/darell-chua/), the founders of [Daqstra](https://www.daqstra.com/).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106987&key=user_uploads/2547322/7ed7475e-d673-4796-9462-d40f72da12ad)

We met while testing liquid rocket engines in the Mojave Desert.

The engines were difficult, but much of the friction came from the infrastructure around them. Before each test, we connected sensors, custom electronics, NI hardware, PLCs, and controllers that were never designed to work together. After each run, the data was scattered across machines, file formats, scripts, and people’s heads.

Before we could learn from one test, we often had to reconstruct what had happened.

After talking with teams building rockets, energy systems, robots, and drones, we kept hearing the same story: **their hardware was advancing faster than the infrastructure used to test it.**

## What We Built

[Watch the demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ykvD67omalI) or visit [daqstra.com](http://daqstra.com).

Daqstra works with the equipment teams already have, including NI/LabVIEW, PLCs, custom DAQ systems, sensors, controllers, and vendor hardware.

* **Daqstra Edge** connects hardware at the test site and records commands alongside the resulting telemetry.
* **Daqstra Hub** stores each run with its configuration, events, notes, and engineering context, making it easier to monitor tests, compare runs, and investigate anomalies.
* **Daqstra API** lets engineers configure hardware and execute repeatable test sequences through software.

Together, these give teams one interface across otherwise incompatible hardware without forcing them to replace their existing stack.

## What We’re Already Doing

We’re working with advanced hardware teams across aerospace, energy, and drones. Our active aerospace programs use Daqstra day to day across fragmented, multi-vendor test environments.

In energy, we’ve signed a pilot with a palm oil processor targeting $100K+ in annual savings by reducing recoverable oil lost through its effluent stream. We’re also helping drone teams unify telemetry, control, and test data across vehicles and ground systems.

## Who We’d Love to Meet

If you lead test, propulsion, integration, validation, or hardware engineering and run frequent instrumented tests, we’d love to talk.

Daqstra is especially useful if your team:

* Works across vendor equipment, PLCs, custom electronics, and in-house software
* Reconfigures its setup between tests or struggles to compare runs
* Relies on a few engineers who understand the entire test environment

We’re initially focused on aerospace, energy, drones, and robotics. If this sounds like your team, reply here or email [**team@daqstra.com**](mailto:team@daqstra.com).

If it sounds like someone you know, we’d appreciate an introduction to the person responsible for test infrastructure, integration, or validation.

**Ad Astra Per Daqstra**

launches.title: Neuromorphic - Building an embodiment-agnostic “brain” that makes robots fast to deploy
launches.tagline: We make robots smarter, and faster to deploy. Starting with wet labs!
launches.body:
Hi everyone! We’re Cem, Ege, and Vatan, the founders of Neuromorphic 👋\
\
**TL;DR** Neuromorphic is building an embodiment-agnostic “brain” that makes robots fast to deploy, and easy to manage through natural interfaces like Slack, email, and phone. Our goal is to make deploying robots in wet labs and other physical industries as easy as onboarding a new employee.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6T0BDyjakmo>\
\
**The Problem**\
To make robotics mainstream, we believe two problems have to be resolved:\
1\. Deployment: Robots are still too slow, expensive, and engineering-intensive to deploy and adapt to new tasks and environments.\
2\. Interaction: Managing and controlling robots remains too technical.\
\
**What We’ve Built**\
Neuromorphic packages sensors, compute, and software into a “brain” that can be attached to any robot body. An onboard LLM orchestrator turns natural-language instructions into workflows made up of reusable robotic skills, such as navigating, picking up an object, opening a refrigerator, or inspecting an area. Individual skills can be of various types; they could be AI models we develop, like Vision-Language Models and Video Action Models, or just plain code. Sensor-based safety loops monitor every action to ensure reliable execution.

We are also giving robots emails, phone numbers, and Slack access to make human-robot interaction more intuitive than using dashboards. The robots then respond to queries and take actions using the onboard LLM.\
\
**Traction**\
Within a week of our first conversation with a leading biotechnology company, we deployed our robot in their wet lab, which is capable of operating autonomously 24/7, and already completed over 1500 tasks.\
\
**The Team**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109550&key=user_uploads/3607343/b28b023b-f328-4c5d-9181-720e96e5b1a3)

\
Cem: Second-time founder and did robotics research at Cambridge University. Previously built LLM routing and training acceleration, and did precision robotics.\
\
Vatan: Maintained multiple open-source robotics libraries, most notably MoveIt, one of the most popular motion-planning frameworks for robotics. Led various teams in robotics startups from Series A to Series C in Japan and Singapore. Deployed over a thousand robots.\
\
Ege: Did Robotics and AI research at Bilkent University. Research fellow at Nanyang Technological University. Published research in top AI and robotics conferences. Won HackMIT in 2024.\
\
Cem and Ege first met as teammates in the FIRST Robotics Competition. They reached out to Vatan for mentorship and robotics advice. We spent the next three years building robots and winning competitions together. We remained close and eventually reunited to start Neuromorphic!\
\
**Ask**\
We're looking for warm intros to wet lab, biotech, and physical-industry operators. If you have a repetitive physical process and have wondered whether a robot could do it, email us at [founders@neuromorphic.vision](mailto:founders@neuromorphic.vision) or [book a call here](https://cal.com/team/neuromorphic/meet-the-founders-of-neuromorphic).

name: Ultrasonium
long_description:
The technologies that define this century, including data centers, rockets, satellites, and robots, are built from complex metal parts. As these systems advance, the parts get harder to make. Past a certain complexity, casting and machining stop working, and the advanced methods that remain are slow, expensive, and hazardous.

Ultrasonium has invented a new manufacturing method to make these critical parts 15x faster and 75% cheaper than the methods they replace, in the U.S. and at scale. Solid metal feedstock goes in and a finished part safely comes out, controlled by a physical AI layer and novel control processes. 

The systems that matter most, in aerospace, energy, and compute, are demanding metal geometries that can't be machined or cast and are too expensive and slow to make with incumbent methods, at a moment when domestic manufacturing capacity is a national priority.

Our founding team has built and innovated some of the most complex engineering systems known to man: quantum computers, superconductors, nuclear reactors, and novel aerospace alloy processing methods.
one_liner: Metal manufacturing, faster, cheaper, and more versatile.

launches.title: Ultrasonium: Shaping the Future of Metal Manufacturing
launches.tagline: We make the world’s most difficult metal parts faster, cheaper, and more versatile.
launches.body:
**The problem**

The technologies that define this century, including data centers, rockets, satellites, robots, etc., are built from complex metal parts. As these systems advance, the parts get harder to make. Past a certain complexity, casting and machining stop working, and the advanced methods that remain are slow, expensive, and limited in the alloys and geometries they can process.

**What we built**

Ultrasonium has invented a new method to make these critical parts. Solid metal feedstock goes in and a finished part comes out, controlled by a Physical AI layer and novel control processes.

We produce near-net-shape complex metal parts up to 15× faster, 75% cheaper, and with far greater alloy versatility than conventional manufacturing methods, at scale in the U.S.

<https://youtu.be/5REHWdzDAhk>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=113464&key=user_uploads/3735756/dbd12c5d-1203-4e50-9939-980a218df45a)

**Why now / why us**

The systems that matter most, in aerospace, defense, energy, and compute, are demanding metal geometries that can’t be machined or cast and are too expensive and slow to make with incumbent methods, at a moment when domestic manufacturing capacity is a national priority.

Our founding team has worked on some of the most difficult engineering systems in the world, including quantum computers, superconductors, nuclear reactors, and advanced aerospace alloy processing. Between the four of us, we have backgrounds in physics, metallurgy, advanced manufacturing, controls, hardware, and commercialization.

Jack Qiu (CEO) completed his PhD in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at MIT and published pioneering quantum computing work in Nature Physics. Chris Carter (CSO) left to join Ultrasonium during the 5th year of his PhD program at MIT after more than six years of research in state-of-the-art metallurgy and materials processing. Alexander Urbanski (Chief Research Officer) previously founded a DOE-funded nuclear startup and was the first hire at Phase3D, where he built and commercialized metal manufacturing monitoring technology. Hunter Brown (VP, Engineering) began working at national labs when he was 15, studied physics at UC Berkeley, and contributed to the ITER fusion reactor.

Manufacturing means choosing suppliers, booking transport, and keeping pulse on new tariffs - to make sure your production is fine. Companies tend to find out about disruptions when things break and cost them millions.

Ekho customers get an early warning AND optimal solution 1-3 weeks ahead of the events. So ships keep moving, production lines keep running, and customer promises get kept.

launches.title: Cosmic Robotics: Autonomous construction on Earth and beyond
launches.tagline: Robotic construction equipment to build a city on Mars. We’re proving the technology by building large-scale infrastructure on Earth — utility-scale solar farms and hyperscale data centers.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We’re [James](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jamesemerick/) and [Lewis](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewis-c-jones/) - co-founders of [Cosmic Robotics](https://www.cosmicrobotics.com). 

**TL;DR**

**We build robotic construction equipment to build a city on Mars**. We’re proving the technology today by building large-scale infrastructure on Earth – utility-scale solar farms and hyperscale data centers. Our first machine, Cosmic-1, has already installed tens of thousands of solar panels in the field and more than doubled the productivity of traditional crews.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_Dl00xlJbcI> 

**❌ The problem**

After working at NASA JPL, SpaceX, and Relativity Space, we believe rockets are no longer the limiting factor to space exploration and that the first humans will land on Mars by 2034. **The new bottleneck is construction**. We won't be sending thousands of construction workers to Mars to build the energy, compute, and housing needed to sustain even a small city. **It has to be built by robots that don't exist yet**.

On Earth we have a similar problem - **we’ve lost the ability to build**. Construction productivity has declined for 50 years while manufacturing and agriculture became 10-15x more productive through automation. **The missing technology is robotic manipulation for the tasks still done by hand**: lifting, placing, fastening.

Meanwhile, there is a generational infrastructure buildout happening right now. **$7 trillion** is going into AI data centers, power, and compute over the next six years, **more than the Apollo Program, Manhattan Project, and Interstate Highway System combined**. 40% of US data center projects are running behind schedule, and the skilled labor shortage is the #1 cause. 

**🤖 What we've built**

Cosmic-1 is a 10,000 lb autonomous robot capable of heavy-lift manipulation. In solar, it picks up 90 lb panels and places them onto racking with millimeter precision in any environment: 100-degree heat, freezing rain, snow, and dust. It seamlessly integrates into existing construction processes. Across tens of thousands of cycles it has more than doubled the labor productivity of solar installation, on some of the largest solar projects in the US.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106899&key=user_uploads/522502/bb5f86ec-a23b-4ffd-a173-87f36ce6fb1c)

**👬 The Team**

We come at this problem from two angles. James (CEO) grew up on construction sites, then spent his career bringing robots to the field with Built Robotics and Autodesk Research. He learned you don't change the oldest industry in the world by disrupting it; you earn your way in by giving crews better tools.

Lewis' (CTO) life ambition is to build a city on Mars. His work at NASA, SpaceX, and Relativity Space spans rocket engines, launch vehicles, satellites, space stations, and, yes, Martian robots. When it became clear the space industry was well on its way to Mars, he went looking for the construction robots. When he didn't find them, we started Cosmic.

We’ve brought together a team of industry experts with experience building robots, rockets, drones, self-driving cars, humanoids, and nuclear reactor operations. We know what it takes to get a machine to show up day-in-day-out on the jobsite.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106899&key=user_uploads/522502/87f30a8e-6f83-490e-8bef-04225d1a525e)

**🚀 What's next**

We're scaling in solar, taking Cosmic-1 into data center construction, and working with NASA on lunar construction robotics. Revenue and data from deployments on Earth train the systems we'll deploy on Mars.

**🙏 Our asks**

1. **Know a hyperscaler or neocloud construction team?** Please connect us.
2. **Share this post** and [follow our journey](https://www.linkedin.com/company/cosmic-robotics/).

👉 Contact us at [james@cosmicrobotics.com](mailto:james@cosmicrobotics.com) | [cosmicrobotics.com](http://cosmicrobotics.com)

launches.title: Praxis AI - Training Data for Robotics
launches.tagline: Praxis offers labs the most diverse environments, SOTA hardware, and rigorous post processing to train their models
launches.body:
**Hey YC!**

We're Rohan, Dev, and Tommy, and we're building Praxis.

**Praxis turns real-world work into training data for robots.**

<https://youtu.be/xri7vyzxW-I?si=L6ZBgLO24OrvYuuH>

**What we do**

Robots learn to act in the physical world by watching humans do the work. We partner with businesses to capture egocentric human demonstration data, the first-person video of how tasks actually get done in factories, warehouses, homes, and other physical work environments, then supply it to the labs and humanoid teams training the next generation of robots. Robotics data is our focus, but since our collection infrastructure overlaps, we're happy to explore other multimodal data too.

**The problem**

Robotics is missing its internet-scale training corpus. LLMs learned from the web, books, code, and the accumulated record of human thought. Robots need the equivalent record of human action: how people pick, pack, clean, assemble, inspect, cook, use tools, recover from mistakes, and move through messy physical environments.

Collecting some of this data is easy. Collecting enough of the right kind is brutally hard, for two reasons.

First, diversity is capped by access. Models only generalise if they've seen the full range of real environments and operators, from a one-person shop to a national-scale industrial operation. Getting in the door across that entire spectrum, and across continents, is a physical-world access problem that most teams can't solve.

Second, it takes two rare skills at once. You have to know what frontier labs need at a technical level, and be able to run demanding physical operations across thousands of real sites, standardising capture and turning fragmented workflows into model-ready data. Few teams have both halves.

**Our solution**

We already run collections across 150 environment types on 5 continents, with diversity from mom-and-pop stores to conglomerates accounting for 3% of a nation's GDP, and a reachable network of 60,000 workers. Depending on the task, we capture egocentric video, stereo-RGB, IMU, wrist-camera views, glove kinematics, haptics, and dense annotations. Everything is delivered calibrated, synced, pose-tracked, QA'd, and PII-scrubbed. We build and deploy custom capture hardware quickly because part of the team operates out of Shenzhen.

**Why us**

Praxis is built to do both hard things at once. We pair robotics research depth (IEEE, NASA JPL) with the ability to actually run demanding operations in the real world, from Fortune 500 supply chains to Parliaments, plus a Shenzhen hardware team. That combination- technical understanding of what labs need plus real physical-world access at scale- is what lets us deliver diverse, model-ready data at a cost and breadth that is irreplaceable.

**Our asks**

1. Intros to anyone working on robotics, embodied AI, or world-models, especially data and research leads. If you need other forms of multimodal data, we're happy to explore that too.
2. If you run a business with interesting physical work (logistics, manufacturing, food, retail, or lab work) and would like to monetize it, we'd love to talk.

You can reach us at [founders@praxisrobotics.io](mailto:founders@praxisrobotics.io) and [rohan@praxisrobotics.io](mailto:rohan@praxisrobotics.io)[ https://www.praxisrobotics.io](https://www.praxisrobotics.io)

launches.body:
History’s greatest ages are named after materials (Stone Age, Bronze Age, Iron Age, Silicon Age, etc.). The next great age is ours to make together.\
\
<https://youtu.be/ysIdrc7mowM>
\
**TL;DR:** We are a team of Stanford, MIT, and Harvard researchers discovering breakthrough materials by training frontier models on decades of unpublished experimental data. **We've already discovered a novel material and drafted a manuscript for publication.**

Industrial R&D teams use us to find scalable application-specific materials that frontier models can't predict. Academic labs turn decades of unpublished data into new papers, citations, and commercialization revenue with us.

**What we do**

We are uncovering novel materials that help industry improve performance at scale and stay top of new regulations. Examples include replacements for PFAS, the "forever chemicals" that are being banned worldwide, and finding a binder for silicon anodes that can survive charging and drop into existing battery manufacturing processes (our cofounder Ian’s work at Sila Nanotechnologies).

**Why we're different**

The materials performance that matters to industry can only be measured in real experiments, but >85% of experimental research is never published. Frontier models train on papers and simulations and miss all the failures sitting in file drawers. We train on that unpublished data through partnerships with labs across the country, and it’s already working: we've already discovered a novel material and drafted a manuscript for publication.

**Who we are**

We are Eric, Ian, and Yankang, collaborators for years on everything from superconductors to cooling textiles, and we lead a team of world-class researchers and commercialization experts.

Eric developed one of the early generative AI approaches for analyzing experimental data (MIT PhD), Ian has brought multiple climate technologies to market, and Yankang led Boston Consulting Group’s AI program, scaling frontier technology to 30,000+ users globally. Advisors: Simon Billinge (UCSB), Mingda Li (MIT), Ashwin Sreenivas (Decagon).

**Our ask**

If you need better materials to drive performance and cost, especially in batteries, semis, membranes, catalysts or pharma, or know an academic lab sitting on experimental data, we'd love an intro: [hello@83sciences.ai](mailto:hello@83sciences.ai)

launches.title: SubVysion: Preventing $150B is wasted construction spending
launches.tagline: Autonomous rovers building the 'Google Maps' of subsurface infrastructure
launches.body:
<https://youtu.be/5IY3vHEJ7J4>

Construction has a mapping problem. Of the $2.2T in annual US construction spending, $150B is wasted due to a lack of subsurface knowledge. All construction starts from the ground up, and more often than not, unexpected assets underneath the surface will hold a construction project back. Whether it's an unknown utility line, unexpected rock layer, or old foundation that wasn’t on any design map, the costs of delays from underground conflicts quickly add up. 

Take utility strikes, when an excavator hits an active utility line. For every dollar spent on the explicit repair cost of that utility line itself, the contractor loses an additional $30 per repair-dollar in project delays, insurance claims, idle work crews, and increased insurance premiums. For a hyperscale project such as data center construction, a single day of delay can cost the cloud-provider up to $14 million dollars for that single day.

In metropolitan areas, maps are incomplete at best and none create a unified picture of critical infrastructure, making excavation especially dangerous when natural gas or electric lines are broken.

Enter SubVysion. We’ve built a fleet of autonomous rovers carrying ground-penetrating radar and other sensors that create a centimeter-accurate map of subsurface infrastructure. Our hardware is the first and the best to map the entirety of US infrastructure. Using our rovers, we comprehensively map construction sites, city streets, and even larger indoor buildings, at 100x better granularity and 10x the speed (with a single rover) compared to our competitors. We process vast amounts of data using machine learning and agents, and output that data into an easy-to-understand 3D scene. 

Who are we? Maxwell Stone was an early ML engineer at Roboflow (YC S20), and Wenson Tang built the world’s smallest and cheapest LiDAR-capable drone for adverse environments. We both studied computer science at the University of Pennsylvania. Together, we’re building SubVysion to map the entirety of America’s subsurface infrastructure.

We’re currently on job sites in Philadelphia and Texas, helping our first market of utility contractors save hundreds of thousands of dollars every year. We’re soon to expand our mapping services to municipalities and energy providers as we scale up our rover fleet and capacity!

If you’re in the energy, infrastructure, or hyperscale construction world, we’d love to hear from you at [founders@subvysion.com](mailto:founders@subvysion.com)!

name: Robocurve
long_description:
Robocurve builds open-source tools and independent benchmarks to measure how well robots can do real-world jobs. Instead of relying on unverified demo videos from frontier labs, we score their models on reproducible benchmarks that anyone can trust.

Today there are no well-run, standardized robotics benchmarks. Labs evaluate in-house, and no independent group has stepped in to run continuous benchmarking as a service. The result is that no one actually knows how good anyone else is, or where the real frontier sits.

Good benchmarks require operating and maintaining physical hardware and real-world setups. Simulation only goes so far, since models that look strong in sim can show large performance gaps once deployed in the real world. Building real-world benchmarks means coordinating job-domain experts, evals engineering, and hands-on robotics all at once.

Frontier labs are targeting general-purpose robotics by 2028, yet the field of robotics evals barely exists. Whoever builds the trusted measure of robot capability becomes the reference everyone relies on. We combine backgrounds in AI evals and robotics to build and grow this field as fast as possible. We already shipped v1 of our open-source framework, Inspect Robots, and ran our first pilot scoring a frontier model on a real robot.
one_liner: Evals for robots

launches.title: Robocurve — Real-World Evaluations of Physical AI
launches.tagline: Real-world evals for robots
launches.body:
Hi, I’m [Jay](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeqcho/), co-founder of [Robocurve](http://robocurve.org). We measure and reports what frontier robots can actually do in the real world.

Our launch video <https://youtu.be/Cjkt2ikvsiQ>

Frontier labs are racing to build general-purpose robots within two years, yet no one knows what today's robots are truly capable of. Demo videos of robots performing narrow, cherry-picked tasks proliferate, but there are no rigorous, continuous, standardized benchmarks for robotics.

Robocurve builds benchmarks for robots and the AI models that control them, to help the world understand how far robotics has come and how fast it's moving. Our benchmarks range from playing Jenga and making a sandwich to constructing a data center.

General-purpose robots could arrive before the end of the decade, with far-reaching implications: accelerated data center buildouts, explosive economic growth from a fully automated economy, and intensified geopolitical competition between the US and China. Real-world evaluations from Robocurve will help clarify the timeline to general-purpose robots so that society can prepare for their arrival well ahead of time.

[Jay](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeqcho/) is a Rhodes Scholar and a top contributor to UK AI Security Institute's Inspect Evals. He has published papers in ICML, EMNLP, ACL, ACM EC and his research has been featured in MIT Technology Review. Previously, he spent time at AWS Bedrock, MATS, and Harvard where he completed his BA and MA with a highest honors thesis on AI and democracy.

If you build robots or AI models, reach out! We'd love to put them to the test. Learn more at [robocurve.org](http://robocurve.org).

launches.body:
We're [Caleb](https://www.linkedin.com/in/caleb-horan) and [Janak](https://www.linkedin.com/in/janak-panthi), PhD roboticists from UT Austin. We've spent a combined 15 years in nuclear, 10 of which deploying autonomous robots at Los Alamos National Lab, and we're building Salem Robotics.\
**TLDR:** Our software turns robots into independent survey and inspection workers at your facility.

[Launch Video](https://youtu.be/7xObOE6knZM)

## **Life and death pain worth $Millions/year**

At every nuclear facility, highly trained radiation-protection teams spend hours each day walking the site, filling out hand-drawn maps, and searching for something life-threatening: radiation. IN THE BEST CASE they find nothing, and still have to return to their posts to transcribe the data into a computer before doing the actual high-value work they were assigned. These surveys are time-consuming, dangerous, expensive, and prone to data inconsistencies that carry direct regulatory consequences.

The same pain exists well beyond nuclear. Whether it's gas-leak inspection or ammonia surveys, similar workflows run across oil, gas, chemical, biological, space, and other hazardous facilities.

## **What we do**

An operator defines the work from a simple dashboard; the robot then navigates the site, handles instruments, opens doors, turns valves, collects measurements, and generates structured, auditable, compliance-ready reports. We're hardware-agnostic, so plants run our software on robots they already own, many of which sit in a closet today as "$200k paperweights, " or we can provide the right robot for the job. Our stack is designed for safety-critical infrastructure and comes with theoretical safety guarantees, exactly what regulators and plant leadership require. Our core manipulation framework was not possible before and is based on **breakthrough founder research** published and presented at the most prestigious IEEE journals and conferences in the world. 

We're already in active contract-scoping conversations across the nuclear industry and oil & gas.

**Our asks**

* Intros to operations or innovation leaders in nuclear or similar hazardous sites (oil, gas, chem, bio, space).
* Advice from founders who've sold into safety-critical industrial environments.
* Sites where routine surveys are frequent, hard to staff, or particularly painful? We'd love to hear about them.

Comments, Emails, and DMs welcome. \

launches.body:
\*\*We're building floating data centers on barges powered by nuclear ships at sea.\*\*

<https://www.youtube.com/embed/unRTV4ZJXts?si=B5E5Z1xGe_NA7FLx>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107426&key=user_uploads/697566/5530961e-115c-4010-b749-b4de1a939afa)


\
**TL;DR:** We move data center campuses offshore, away from communities, onto standardized barges we build on a single manufacturing line. That gets us near-free cooling, no interconnection queue, no local opposition, and 2x faster deployment. First gas-powered pilot ready by 2028.

Why now: AI has created unprecedented demand for compute and power that cannot be satisfied onshore.

* Grid interconnection timelines are **approaching a decade**.
* Data centers drive up the local cost of electricity, rent and land, and make water scarce. Community opposition rising from those reasons has **killed more than half of planned projects** since 2025.

What we're building: standardized, plug-and-play data center barges, built on one manufacturing line and towed to site. Moving offshore gives us:

* **No interconnection queue and no community impact** because our system operates standalone.
* More **scalable architecture** that offers **faster deployment** and tighter-controlled deliverability due to centralized construction and repeated site licensing
* **Lower energy cost** due to **less capacity overbuild** than onshore behind-the-meter and **cheaper financing** for repeatable manufacturing compared to on-site construction (financing = \~2/3 of the lifetime cost of a nuclear project)
* Virtually **free cooling** from seawater.

Traction: We already have early partnerships in place across the two hardest parts of this build:

* **Offshore design & construction:** working with established offshore barge designer/builders.
* **Nuclear power:** partnerships with multiple SMR vendors.

Why us: We're a two-founder team out of MIT with the exact mix this needs.

* [@Emile Germonpre](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3640819) has a PhD in nuclear engineering.
* [@Dimitris Koutentakis](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/697566) has a BS/MEng in EECS, an MS in Mechanical Engineering, and an MBA, all from MIT, with deep connections to the Greek shipping industry.

**Our ask:** We're looking for intros to decision-makers in compute infrastructure or data center development we can sell to, VPs of Data Center Construction, Directors of Infrastructure, and hyperscaler / neocloud teams. If that's you or someone you know, reach out at [dimitris@atomarine.co](mailto:dimitris@atomarine.co) & [emile@atomarine.co](mailto:emile@atomarine.co).

name: Hemlock
long_description:
Every serious robotics lab is bottlenecked on the same thing: demonstration data. The field has converged on egocentric video and hand pose as the substrate, and both are now cheap to collect at scale. What neither of them contains is force. A video of someone picking up an egg and a video of someone picking up a rock are nearly identical in pixel space and nearly identical in joint angles. They differ almost entirely in a quantity nobody is recording. Policies trained without it learn geometry and inherit no sense of touch.

Hemlock closes that gap at the source. Our device, the Bracelet, is a wrist-worn surface EMG band that reads the electrical activity of the forearm muscles that actually drive the hand, which means it recovers contraction force directly rather than inferring it from motion. This distinction is the whole thesis: force cannot be reconstructed downstream of kinematics, because a hand squeezing hard isometrically and a hand resting can occupy the identical pose. Muscle signal is the only non-invasive channel that separates them.
one_liner: Force-sensing wristband for training robotic AI
